ufo (URL utilities, TypeScript under src/, every module re-exported from src/index.ts) can add or overwrite query parameters with withQuery(input, query) and read them with getQuery(input), both in src/utils.ts, but it has no way to drop parameters selectively. Add, beside withQuery, and export from the package entry src/index.ts a function filterQuery(input: string, predicate: (key: string, value: string | string[]) => boolean): string that returns input keeping only the query parameters for which predicate returns true. Its rules: an input that contains no "?" is returned exactly as given (filterQuery("file:///C:/x", () => false) is "file:///C:/x", not normalized). Otherwise predicate is called once for each key of getQuery(input), in that order, with the decoded key and the value getQuery gives it (a string, or an array of strings for a repeated key, so a repeated key is kept or dropped as a whole), and the URL is rebuilt the way withQuery rebuilds it: filterQuery(input, () => true) equals withQuery(input, {}) for every input that contains "?"; protocol, auth, host, path and fragment are kept as withQuery keeps them; the kept parameters are encoded as withQuery encodes them; and the "?" is left out when no parameter remains. Examples: filterQuery("/foo?bar=1&baz=2", (key) => key !== "bar") is "/foo?baz=2"; filterQuery("/foo?bar=1", (key) => key !== "bar") is "/foo"; filterQuery("/foo?a=1&a=2&bar=3#frag", (key) => key !== "bar") is "/foo?a=1&a=2#frag"; filterQuery("https://example.com/p?q=%20x&bar=1", (key, value) => value !== "1") is "https://example.com/p?q=+x". What must not change: every existing export keeps its name and its behaviour for every input, in particular withQuery, getQuery, parseQuery, stringifyQuery, parseURL and stringifyParsedURL return exactly what they return today (for example withQuery("/x?bar", {}) stays "/x?bar", withQuery("/foo?", {}) stays "/foo" and withQuery("/p?x=1&&bar=2&", {}) stays "/p?x=1&bar=2"), and getQuery and parseQuery still return an object that does not inherit from Object.prototype and still ignore __proto__ and constructor keys. The tests are vitest files under test/, with the query utilities in test/query.test.ts. Add regression tests for filterQuery to the project's existing test suite. The project's tests run with npx vitest run --typecheck (npm test runs pnpm lint first; on the unchanged base under this install, prettier already reports src/punycode.ts, so lint is not part of the required test command).
